old.name: Arco da Vila — neoclassical over Moorish
old.label: GATE
old.hook: Two civilisations in one passageway, a stork's nest on top
old.text: Two civilisations in one passageway, a stork's nest on top free WALK-IN All day Bishop Francisco Gomes do Avelar commissioned the neoclassical arch in 1812 as part of the long post-1755 reconstruction; the Genoese architect Francisco Xavier Fabri designed it. Inside the tunnel passageway, the original 11th-century Moorish horseshoe gateway survives intact. The niche above holds a white marble statue of Saint Thomas Aquinas. White storks have nested on top for generations — the bell tower carries a single enormous nest. Where Cidade Velha — main entrance

old.name: Sé Cathedral de Faro
old.label: CATHEDRAL
old.hook: Four religions, one site — the bell tower view over the Ria Formosa is the lesson
old.text: Four religions, one site — the bell tower view over the Ria Formosa is the lesson EUR 4-5 WALK-IN Morning Afonso III took Faro in 1249; the existing mosque was immediately consecrated as the cathedral, the third building on a site that had already been a Roman temple and a Visigothic basilica. The medieval interior was destroyed by Essex in 1596; the nave was rebuilt in the 17th century in the austere Tuscan order. The 18th-c. Baroque organ and the azulejo panels on the side walls are the principal interior features. Climb the bell tower early — the view over the Ria Formosa is the best single landscape lesson in southern Portugal. Stork nests crowd the upper ledges. Where Cidade Velha

old.text: Roman mosaic of the Ocean (3rd c.) inside a former convent EUR 2-3 WALK-IN Afternoon The municipal museum occupies a 16th-century domed Renaissance convent built on what was once the Jewish quarter. Collections span prehistory to the 20th century: a remarkable 3rd-c. Roman Mosaic of the Ocean (found 1976), 9th–13th-c. Islamic domestic artefacts, medieval Christian items, 16th–19th-c. religious paintings, work by the local painter Carlos Filipe Porfírio. The cloister, with its central well and azulejo panels, is one of the most tranquil spaces in the city at 16:00. Where Cidade Velha

old.text: «Pára aqui a considerar que a este estado hás-de chegar» EUR 2 WALK-IN All day Behind the Rococo Igreja do Carmo (gilded talha dourada from Brazilian gold), a 4 × 6 m chapel built in 1816 from the bones of more than a thousand Carmelite friars excavated from the parish cemetery in the convent's rear garden. 1,245 skulls. The inscription above the entrance reads: «Pára aqui a considerar que a este estado hás-de chegar» — "Stop here and consider that you will reach this state." Geometric precision; sober where Évora's is chaotic. Where Largo do Carmo

old.name: Teatro Municipal de Faro (Lethes)
old.label: THEATRE
old.hook: Italianate horseshoe theatre · «monet oblectando» — "it instructs with amusement"
old.text: Italianate horseshoe theatre · «monet oblectando» — "it instructs with amusement" EUR 5-25 BOOK Evening Built 1605 as the Jesuit Colégio de Santiago Maior (under Bishop Mascarenhas — the same bishop whose library Essex took eleven years before). After the Jesuit expulsion (1759), the building passed through royal hands and survived the desecrations of Junot's troops (1807). Bought at auction in 1843 by Lázaro Doglioni , a Venetian doctor who set out to build a theatre comparable to La Scala. The Teatro Lethes opened on 4 April 1845 — Queen Maria II's birthday. Latin motto on the façade: «monet oblectando» , "it instructs with amusement." Damaged in a storm and reopened 22 February 2026 with a Guitar Festival; now run by ACTA — A Companhia de Teatro do Algarve. Three horseshoe balconies, red velvet, extraordinarily intimate for a city of this size. Where Faro Centro

old.name: Ruínas Romanas de Milreu — Estói
old.label: ROMAN
old.hook: Intact mosaic floors and a fish-cult temple
old.text: Intact mosaic floors and a fish-cult temple EUR 2-3 WALK-IN Morning The Roman site of Milreu sits in the village of Estói, ten kilometres north of Faro. Once Ossonoba, the antecedent of Faro itself, it preserves a 1st-to-4th-century villa-and-temple complex with intact mosaic floors (including a remarkable fish-themed mosaic in the temple-bathhouse) and walls still standing several metres high. Combine with a visit to the Pousada Palácio de Estói next door for a long historical morning. Where Estói — 10 km north
